title: Scientists Solved How a Gut Bacterium Triggers Colon Cancer
hook: Researchers cracked a long-standing mystery — how a common gut bacterium's toxin damages the colon and drives cancer — and used that insight to design a decoy protein that blocked it in mice.
key_points: A bacterial toxin long associated with colorectal cancer works by first binding to a receptor called claudin-4 on colon cells.
That binding gives the toxin access to attack the cells' protective barrier, setting up inflammation and tumor growth.
Researchers used this newly identified weak point to design a decoy protein that successfully blocked the toxin in mice.
The discovery could pave the way for new therapies to prevent inflammation and colon tumors, though it's still at the mouse stage.
content_html: A bacterial toxin long linked to colorectal cancer has kept scientists guessing about exactly how it does its damage. A new study says it's solved that mystery.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, the toxin first binds to a receptor called claudin-4 on colon cells, and that binding is what gives it access to attack the cells' protective barrier — setting off the inflammation and tumor growth associated with colorectal cancer. Having identified that weak point, the research team designed a decoy protein that successfully blocked the toxin in mice. It's still an animal-stage result, but pinpointing the exact mechanism opens a clear path toward therapies that could prevent this kind of damage in people, rather than just treating cancer after it's already formed.

related.title: A Drug for 'Undruggable' Pancreatic Cancer
related.hook: A new drug, daraxonrasib, hits a KRAS mutation long thought 'undruggable' and nearly doubled survival in a trial of advanced pancreatic cancer — a hard-to-treat disease.

related.title: Cancer Screenings Worth Knowing
related.hook: Screening looks for cancer before symptoms start — and for a few common cancers, that early catch dramatically improves the odds.
